answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so a claim receives weight only through paths that remain connected to trusted anchors. A sybil cluster with few links to honest nodes has low conductance: most walks starting inside it stay internal, limiting its influence outside. Under capped per-anchor contributions, min-cut transitivity bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting weight by its external cut, rather than its number of identities; orchard, raven, and zephyr are labels, not independent trust.
